title: Work contracted out with the Civil Service Commission’s approval
question: How much work did the Commission approve departments to contract out rather than give to City employees, by department, and for how long?
finding: The Commission’s minutes from 5 August 2024 to 2 February 2026 print tables listing 282 proposed personal-services contracts worth $3.03 billion, all entered as new requests; the Commission’s packets for the same meetings show that about a quarter were amendments of earlier approvals, so for those the minutes’ amount may be the cumulative ceiling rather than the amount added, and the total may count earlier approvals again. Airport Commission accounts for $778.4 million across 28 contracts, Public Health for $713.2 million across 66 and Public Utilities Commission for $564.8 million across 46. Over the whole period from November 2022 the minutes carry 160 agenda items on such contracts. The tables print no reason for contracting out; the request forms, which do, are read in the screen of contracting-out requests (csc_records).
how: Rows of the contract tables printed in the Commission’s adopted minutes (contract number, department, amount, type of approval, duration), as collected in the table of Commission actions. Amounts are added up by department as printed; 0 rows with an unreadable amount are left out, and a full stop printed in place of a comma is read as a comma. Department names are matched to the payroll’s where the wording allows. The length is the middle duration in months. Ranked by amount.
limits: Contracting out with the Commission’s approval is the route the Charter provides; approval of a ceiling is not spending, and many contracts are never drawn in full. The action recorded for a table applies to the whole agenda item, and single contracts within it can be continued or withdrawn, so some listed amounts were not approved at that meeting. The reason for each request is not in the tables. The minutes print tables only from the middle of 2024; earlier approvals appear as text. Contracts awarded without competition are a different matter, covered under waivers and exceptions.

sources.t: San Francisco Civil Service Commission: adopted minutes, November 2022 to October 2026 (the latest of 81)
